_readme: Mission Tutor script. One short message per line (Next shows the next one). Wrap key words in **double stars** to highlight them; numbers are highlighted automatically. {placeholders} are live numbers (see TutorDialogueManager.context). A step ends when its 'until' happens.

say: Welcome, Director! Floods keep hitting farms in **West Africa**.
Our job: build a small **satellite** that can spot them in time.
We have ${budget}M to spend and the satellite must weigh under {mass_limit} kg.
Use **WASD** to walk and the **mouse** to look around.
Walk up to the **Briefing** screen and press **E** to read it.
The farmers need fresh pictures every {max_revisit} days. Press **E** to close the screen.
Now look at a **part** on the shelves. A card on the right compares it for you.
steps.todo: Look at a part on a shelf

say: Every part has a **plus** and a **minus**. Press **E** to install the one you want.
Watch the **resources** on the left. They change with every choice.
**Green** is fine. **Amber** means careful. **Red** means trouble.
Tip: **precise pointing** keeps our pictures sharp. Try installing it.
The **Advisors** screen lists any problems. Have a look.
Now open the **Mission Console** to choose an orbit and a rocket.
Cheaper rockets save money but carry less. Pick one that fits.
When the resources look green, press **LAUNCH**!
We've reached orbit! Below us is **Africa** and our four farm regions.
Power, memory and passes over Africa are all **limited**. Choose carefully.
Open the **Observation Console** on the left wall.
Choose a region marked **IN VIEW**.
Remember: every scan uses **power** and fills our **memory**.
Scan what you can, then press **END CAMPAIGN**.
steps.todo: Scan the regions, then end the campaign

say: Welcome to the **ground station**! We have {collected} GB of pictures to bring home.
But the satellite is only in range for about {contact} minutes a day.
Choose what comes down first: **floods** or **crops**. Then press **START PASS**.
steps.todo: Set a priority, then press START PASS

say: Here it comes! Watch the dishes follow the satellite.
The pictures are home! Out of the window are the farms we photographed.
Now let's turn those pictures into **warnings** for farmers.
Open the **Analysis Workstation** on the left wall.
Click every **blue** plot. Blue means flooded.
**Grey** plots have no pictures. We can't know what's there.
Choose how to warn people, then press **DELIVER REPORT**.
steps.todo: Mark the flooded plots and deliver

concepts.payload: This is our **camera**. Better cameras see more, but make bigger files.
concepts.solar: **Solar panels** make our power. Everything else needs it.
concepts.battery: The **battery** keeps us running in Earth's shadow.
concepts.comms: The **radio** sends pictures home. Faster radios use more power.
concepts.computer: The **computer** stores pictures until we can send them.
concepts.adcs: **Pointing** aims the camera. Bad pointing means blurry pictures.
concepts.propulsion: The **thruster** keeps us in the right orbit.
concepts.thermal: **Thermal control** keeps the battery warm in the cold of space.

reactions.say: Excellent detail! But these pictures take up a lot more **storage**.
Smaller pictures. Easier to send home, but less detail.
A fast radio! More pictures reach Earth, but it uses more **power**.
A cheap radio. Fine for small pictures, but big ones may get **stuck in space**.
Bigger solar wings: about **twice the power**. A bit heavier though.
Light and simple, but they don't make much **power**.
A bigger battery. We'll get through the dark side of every orbit.
Great choice! Almost every picture will be **sharp**.
Careful: with basic pointing, many pictures will be **blurry**.
Powerful, but it needs about **10 W** while firing. Watch the power.
The battery stays warm, but heaters use about **4 W** of power.
A smart computer: it sends only the useful parts of each picture.
Our own rocket! But it costs ${rocket_cost}M. That money can't go elsewhere.
Good choice! We've saved money. Just remember: this ride can't carry as much.
We'll pass over the farms every {revisit} days, always in daylight.
Easy to reach, but we'd only see the farms every {revisit} days.
Too heavy for this rocket! Lighten the satellite or pick a bigger rocket.
We're running out of **money**. Over budget means no mission.
We're nearly **too heavy**. Every kilogram counts.
Our parts need more **power** than the panels can make.
The battery can't last through Earth's **shadow**.
We'll collect more pictures than our **radio** can send home.
Well done! That decision has moved our mission forward.
Now we'll see the farms often enough to catch floods in time.
Power is back in the **green**. Well done!
Our radio can now send home everything we collect.
We can't launch yet. Check the **red** resources on the left.
We can launch, but the mission will struggle. Press **LAUNCH** again to go anyway.
Nice pictures! That scan used {scan_gb} GB. Memory: {stored} of {storage} GB.
**Clouds!** Our camera can't see through them. Try again on another pass.
Our memory is filling up: {stored} of {storage} GB.
Memory **full**! New pictures are being lost.
That was our last pass. Time to **end the campaign**.
That region isn't below us right now. Wait until it says **IN VIEW**.
Floods first. If time runs out, crop pictures will wait.
Crops first. Good for planning, but flood warnings may come late.
We collected plenty of pictures, but the link couldn't send them all. {left_onboard} GB is still in space.
Well done! Every picture made it home.
First choose how to warn people: alert, map, report or dashboard.
An **alert** goes straight to farmers' phones. Fast!
A **flood map** shows officials where to send help.
A **crop report** helps plan the season, but it's slow for floods.
A **dashboard** keeps everyone updated, if someone is watching.
Well done! You found {flood_found} of {flood_total} floods and warned people in time.
Report sent. You found {flood_found} of {flood_total} floods. Some farmers were missed.
Report sent, but only {flood_found} of {flood_total} floods were found.
{unseen_flood} flooded plots were in the **grey** areas. Those farmers got no warning.
Good choice. Now press **SCAN** to take the pictures.
